sensitivity.name: LOSO 15 iterations
sensitivity.summary: Cellular-immune core (3 endpoints) + supportive CRP retained 15/15 protective LOSO retention in both comparators (cholecystectomy and hernia repair)

sensitivity.name: Sigma-grid widening
sensitivity.summary: All three core endpoints retained significance after calibration vs hernia at sigma = 0.10, 0.20, 0.30; vs cholecystectomy at sigma = 0.20; at sigma = 0.30 vs chole, all three retained protective direction without individual significance. CRP retained significance vs hernia across all sigma levels and lost significance vs chole already at sigma = 0.10.

sensitivity.name: Lookback variation (90/365/unlimited outer; 30-day inner skip)
sensitivity.summary: Vs cholecystectomy: 18/9/12 of 30 endpoints significant after empirical calibration. Vs hernia repair: 12/18/15 of 30 endpoints.

sensitivity.name: Beta secondary window (1-3650 days)
sensitivity.summary: 23/30 vs cholecystectomy and 16/30 vs hernia repair significant after empirical calibration. The beta cholecystectomy increment is dominated by acute hepatobiliary-recovery dynamics (1-30 days), not appendix-specific biology — motivates postacute primary frame.

sensitivity.name: Surveillance intensity bound (per-endpoint App/Comparator measurement-event-count ratios)
sensitivity.summary: Appendectomy patients accrued comparable or higher measurement-event counts than hernia-repair patients across postacute windows (App/Hernia ratio >=1.08 for each core endpoint in 91-365 d and 1-3 yr windows). Vs cholecystectomy, appendectomy patients accrued fewer long-term measurements.
